Mini-Project Presentation & Viva Guide

Complete PowerPoint slide breakdown, system architecture, and frequently asked Viva questions with answers.

SLIDE 1

Project Title & Objective

  • Title: Autonomous AI-Powered Online Examination Proctoring System (Sentinel AI).
  • Objective: To develop a client-side, zero-latency automated proctoring platform that guarantees exam integrity without expensive human invigilators.
  • Scope: Real-time Computer Vision facial pose tracking, prohibited device detection, acoustic speech monitoring, and browser lockdown.
SLIDE 2

Problem Statement & Motivation

  • Post-Pandemic Shift: Shift to remote online examinations created widespread academic integrity issues.
  • Human Proctoring Limitations: Human proctors suffer from cognitive fatigue, high latency, cannot monitor more than 5-10 students simultaneously, and cost significant money.
  • Existing AI Issues: Heavy server-side video streaming causes high bandwidth costs and privacy concerns.
  • Our Solution: Edge AI proctoring running directly in the browser via WebAssembly & WebGL.
SLIDE 3

System Architecture & Workflow

  • Input Layer: User Webcam Stream (640x480 @ 30fps) + Microphone Stream (Web Audio API).
  • Computer Vision Pipeline: MediaPipe FaceMesh (478 3D facial landmarks) for Head Pose (Yaw, Pitch, Roll) and Gaze Tracking.
  • Object Recognition Pipeline: MobileNetV2 COCO-SSD running asynchronously every 500ms for smartphone and book detection.
  • Acoustic Analysis: Real-time Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) analysis to filter ambient noise and detect voice frequencies (100Hz–3000Hz).
  • Browser Security Layer: Page Visibility API, Fullscreen Lock, DevTools shortcut blockers, and window blur listeners.
  • Evaluation & Scoring Engine: Dynamic Trust Score decrement algorithm with automated photographic snapshot evidence logging.
SLIDE 4

Technology Stack

  • Frontend Core: HTML5, Vanilla JavaScript (ES2024 Modules), Modern Vanilla CSS Design System.
  • AI / Machine Learning Frameworks: Google MediaPipe Tasks Vision, TensorFlow.js (TFJS).
  • Web APIs: WebRTC MediaDevices, Web Audio API, Page Visibility API, Fullscreen API, HTML5 Canvas.
  • Bundler / Runtime: Vite Dev Server, WebAssembly (Wasm) acceleration.
SLIDE 5

Key Features & Differentiators

  • 100% Client-Side Privacy: Video is processed on the candidate's device; no raw video streams are transmitted to servers.
  • Sub-30ms Latency: Real-time detection with immediate warning chimes and toasts.
  • Anti-Cheating Forensic Snapshots: Captures high-resolution watermarked evidence whenever a violation occurs.
  • Integrated Viva Sandbox: Built-in live testing tab allows evaluators to verify each AI sensor on demand.
SLIDE 6

Viva Questions & Technical Answers

  • Q: How do you calculate Head Pose (Looking Left/Right)?
    A: We compute the horizontal offset ratio between the 3D nose tip landmark (Point 1) and the midpoint between the left outer eye (Point 33) and right outer eye (Point 263). If the yaw angle exceeds ±18°, a gaze deviation is flagged.
  • Q: How does phone detection work in the browser without freezing the UI?
    A: We run TensorFlow.js MobileNetV2 COCO-SSD asynchronously inside requestAnimationFrame / decoupled setInterval timers using WebGL GPU shaders.
  • Q: What happens if a student switches tabs or presses Alt+Tab?
    A: The Page Visibility API detects the `visibilitychange` state change and `window.blur` event, immediately triggering a -15 penalty and logging a timestamped violation.
  • Q: How do you prevent false positives from normal blinks or background noise?
    A: We implement temporal smoothing and a grace period (e.g., candidate must look away for > 2.5 seconds or noise must sustain across 25 consecutive audio frames) before logging a penalty.
